en.headline: Two of three dogs in Yuen Long fatal attack case are microchipped
en.dek: The AFCD said it is trying to contact the registered owners, who may face prosecution if evidence shows they failed in their responsibilities.
body: The Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department said on Monday that two of the three stray dogs captured in an overnight operation in Yuen Long have microchips. The animals are believed to be linked to the fatal attack on a 27-year-old woman on Pok Wai South Road on Saturday night.
Officers said they are attempting to contact the registered owners. If there is sufficient evidence that the owners failed to fulfil their responsibilities, prosecution may follow.

The department also conducted another joint operation with police on Pok Wai South Road in the afternoon and identified one further stray dog that has not yet been captured. Teams continued to patrol nearby villages and checked the microchips of dogs kept by warehouses and logistics firms in the area.

Roundtable lawmaker Mark Chong called on the government to consider restricting the feeding of stray dogs, saying unmanaged feeding can cause packs to form and increase neighbourhood risks. Yuen Long district councillor Allan Wong described the latest attack as an isolated case.

zh.headline: 元朗致命狗襲兩隻狗有晶片 漁護署嘗試聯絡飼主
zh.dek: 漁護署表示正嘗試聯絡登記飼主，若有足夠證據顯示飼主未盡責任，或會提出檢控。
body: 漁農自然護理署周一表示，在元朗通宵行動中捕獲的三隻流浪狗當中，有兩隻植入晶片。該些狗隻相信與周六晚蒲台南路一名27歲女子遭襲擊致死的案件有關。
漁護署人員表示正嘗試聯絡登記飼主。若有足夠證據顯示飼主未有履行責任，或會提出檢控。
漁護署下午再與警方在蒲台南路進行聯合行動，發現另一隻流浪狗，但尚未能捕獲。人員繼續在附近村落巡邏，並檢查倉庫及物流公司飼養犬隻的晶片資料。
立法會議員莊家彬呼籲政府考慮限制餵飼流浪狗，指無管理的餵飼會令狗隻聚集成群，增加社區風險。元朗區議員黃偉傑則認為今次襲擊屬個別事件。
